headline: Sixth straight down day as AI spending doubts rattle markets
body: Thursday's close extended Wall Street's longest losing streak in months: the S&P 500 fell 2% to 7,175.83, the Dow dropped 2.2% to 49,097.06, and the Nasdaq Composite slid 2.3% to 23,879.20, the sixth consecutive down session. The VIX jumped nearly 16% to 28.44, its highest close in two weeks, a sharper fear signal than the index moves alone suggest. The proximate driver is a renewed round of scrutiny over AI data-center spending and whether the capital being poured into the buildout will pay off, the same worry that drove a sharper rout earlier in the month. Notably, the 10-year Treasury yield eased slightly to just above 5%, consistent with some haven-seeking even as risk assets sold off, rather than a simple rates-driven selloff.

Not everything was risk-off: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut on Thursday priced at $83, opened above $111, and still closed up about 17% at $97.17 despite fading from the open, a sign that appetite for individual growth stories hasn't vanished even as the broader tape sours on AI capex. Retail-sentiment chatter was thin and inconsistent in today's search results, so this read leans more on index-level price action and the capex/valuation narrative than on confirmed social-media positioning. Friday's premarket pointed to continued softness following the sixth straight decline, suggesting the cautious, show-me tone around AI infrastructure spending is carrying into the new session rather than reversing.
